title: LUA-12 (service call), LUA-15 (structured failure), LUA-16 (runtime error capture) need production code changes + tests, not just tests
symptom: LUA-12: call_service.zig gates correctly and, in simulation mode, performs a genuine simulated call. Outside simulation it returns a hardcoded '{}'/200 no-op and never consults service_catalog.zig's fully-implemented ServiceCatalog.lookup, which has zero callers anywhere in host_api. LUA-15: platformFail stores reason/details/explicit_failure into ordinary script-writable Lua globals (__failure_reason__ etc.) -- the same forgery class __limiter__ has -- and nothing reads them back; executeSource never checks them after a failed pcall, so an explicit platform.fail() looks identical to any other runtime error to the caller. LUA-16: no stack trace capture exists (design section 21.2's lua_getstack/lua_getinfo walk has no counterpart); events.zig's ScriptErrorPayload/EventRecord types are correctly built but have zero construction call sites -- pure dead types.
root_cause: LUA-12's non-simulation path and ServiceCatalog integration were deferred by design during the simulation-first implementation pass. LUA-15's globals-based signaling was a placeholder never migrated to the registry-based anti-forgery pattern host_context.zig already established for capabilities. LUA-16 depends on LUA-15's fix landing first (the executor needs to distinguish explicit failure from runtime error before it can label captured errors correctly) and on LUA-08's instruction-count limiter existing (for the instruction-count-at-failure field), so was never independently started.
acceptance_criteria: LUA-12: decide whether ServiceCatalog becomes reachable from ExecutionContext and call lookup() to validate svc_id / resolve endpoint before any real HTTP path; either implement a genuine non-simulation HTTP call or explicitly scope it out as future work with simulation as the only tested path; change return shape to a table per design section 17.1 if still the intended contract; tests for service-found+granted, service-not-found, capability-denied, HTTP-error paths

LUA-12 (deadline-awareness, carried over from ISS-0169/GH-495 Step 2b rework, src/design/iss0169-lua08-09-10-limiter-wiring.md section 11 item 1): whatever HTTP client call_service.zig gains MUST be deadline-aware / cancellable against the same watchdog budget LUA-10's WatchdogState tracks -- e.g. pass the remaining timeout into the client's request call, bound its connect/read timeouts to the remaining watchdog budget, or use a client library supporting request cancellation. Without this, a real outbound HTTP call can block past the script's configured timeout with no way for the host to unblock it early (LUA-10's watchdog can only detect-and-flag before/after the call, per its own documented scope limit -- it cannot forcibly abort an in-flight blocking syscall). This is a hard design input for LUA-12, not an optional nice-to-have -- CODE-DESIGNER must account for it up front rather than discovering it after LUA-12 ships.

LUA-15: move the three failure globals into LUA_REGISTRYINDEX following host_context.zig's established pattern; read them back in executeSource after a failed pcall and distinguish explicit failure from runtime error in ScriptResult; tests proving platform.fail terminates with the given reason/details AND that explicit failure is distinguishable from an uncaught runtime error

LUA-16: implement captureStackTrace via lua_getstack/lua_getinfo; after a failed pcall that is not an explicit failure, construct a ScriptErrorPayload with message/stack trace/instruction count (depends on LUA-08 landing)/capability snapshot; surface this on ScriptResult; tests per design section 21.4 (division by zero, nil access, stack trace has real frame info, instruction count recorded, capability state recorded, explicit-failure-vs-runtime-error distinguishable -- shared test surface with LUA-15)
Sequencing note: LUA-16 should land after or alongside LUA-15 (shared executeSource branch and ScriptResult shape change) and after LUA-08 (instruction-count field)
All three requirements restored to RELEASED with evidence, or the residual gap documented
notes: Split out of GH-495/ISS-0169 during WF03-GH495-20260808 per the human-operator-confirmed decision to batch that run's 9-requirement scope into 3 deliverable pieces (limiters LUA-08/09/10 tackled in that run; this issue and a sibling ISS-0624 for LUA-11/13 cover the remaining 6). See docs/issues/ISS-0169.json for the full original gap assessment this issue's scope was carved from.
